purpose: Research-backed hypotheses for a fresh Snake26 agent. No rule is implemented or promoted until controlled testing.

evidence_stages.4: Promoted after fresh diverse league-like validation

rules.title: Avoid provably fatal next actions
rules.if_state: A candidate step enters a currently occupied body/tail cell, or two heads may reach one destination, under 2026 simultaneous game mechanics.
rules.then_hypothesis: Separate engine-verified certain collision from probabilistic head exposure, and account for simultaneously moving tails; do not ban every current tail cell.
rules.counterexample: A surviving snake can move onto its own OLD tail coordinate when that segment vacates; recorded victim events do not expose the dead snake's attempted move.
rules.next_experiment: Directly compare chosen move-pair transitions, tail release during growth, and respawn/kill ordering against the authoritative current 2026 compiled game engine before certifying a deterministic fatal-action filter.
rules.falsification: An engine-verifiable transition contradicts the chosen-move safety prediction (including simultaneous tail vacating or contested apple growth).

rules.title: Estimate head threat jointly with escape-space scarcity
rules.if_state: An opponent head is <=3 toroidal cells away, especially with <=1 presently unoccupied neighboring cell.
rules.then_hypothesis: Include opponent-head reach and locally available escape directions as joint danger features; do not automatically flee.
rules.counterexample: Simple one-step head cones cover normal observed movements, but adding them to route-area predictors improved held-out league AUC only marginally with interval crossing zero. A geometric reach cone includes collision-impossible moves and can overstate actual opponent risk.
rules.next_experiment: Test empirically observed head-to-head and opponent next-move frequencies by body length, exact heading, position, and contested apple state in fresh whole league games; compare calibrated risk predictors and agent ablations.
rules.falsification: In matched held-out league states the joint features do not predict death or loss of safe routes over simpler baselines.

rules.title: Preserve future routes rather than maximize immediate free neighbors
rules.if_state: Multiple apparently safe moves lead to different future reachable regions or narrow corridors.
rules.then_hypothesis: Prefer moves that maintain tail-aware future connectivity when the near-term cost is reasonable.
rules.counterexample: Moving-tail search showed only a small, uncertain held-out AUC gain over frozen flood-fill; top, middle and bottom snakes selected highest-score modeled moves at similar rates. High predicted reachable area is NOT a proven best first action.
rules.next_experiment: Validate whether opponent-aware route scores improve independent later-season league AUC (the current +0.015 held-out advantage is uncertain), then compare simpler frozen flood-fill, moving-tail and head-cone features in controlled opponent-diverse ablations.
rules.falsification: Dynamic connectivity fails to predict survival or gives poorer league results than a static or simpler heuristic.

rules.title: Target contest-adjusted safe food, not simply nearest apple
rules.if_state: Two snakes can reach a visible apple, and static safe-path ordering differs from toroidal geometric distance.
rules.then_hypothesis: Estimate safe arrival times, contested landing-head risks, and post-apple escape space before committing.
rules.counterexample: Static path distances can misidentify future routes because opponent and own body cells move; trial relationships may not transfer to league.
rules.next_experiment: Use body-aware path and opponent intercept timing on held-out league games, then controlled paired-seed agents; a length tie-break improved predicted captured-by accuracy, but is not an action reward.
rules.falsification: Contest-aware arrival calculations do not improve held-out league prediction or controlled capture/retained-growth rates.

rules.title: Optimize retained growth and competitive placement, not raw apple count
rules.if_state: An apple is available, but pursuit adds measurable collision or enclosure risk.
rules.then_hypothesis: Value apple gain against probability-weighted loss of existing length and reduced opportunity to place first.
rules.counterexample: Final length and placement are both outcomes; correlation cannot establish how much risk to accept or whether chasing was deliberate.
rules.next_experiment: Estimate food capture, death/reset hazard and final retained length conditional on body length, phase, opponents and available actions.
rules.falsification: Risk-adjusted scoring fails to increase league-like first-place outcomes relative to food-first and safety-first policies.

rules.title: Use relative strength and opponent paths when contesting cells
rules.if_state: An opponent can approach the same cell or apple in the next few turns.
rules.then_hypothesis: Measure each possible move's exposure to reachable opponent heads and relative length; consider state-dependent confrontation versus retreat, but do not infer intent, legality or an approved attack rule.
rules.counterexample: Top-ranked snakes entered possible head-contest cells more frequently overall, but once conditioned on having a shorter-only contest opportunity, top 68.2% and bottom 73.7% (only 19 eligible bottom moves). Growth and opportunity confound apparent aggression; dead-on-first-step choices are missing.
rules.next_experiment: Separate opportunities from decisions, stratify by exact relative body length, opponent heading and alive-at-next-frame censoring, audit 2026 head-to-head collision transitions and contested apples, then validate across fresh league seasons.
rules.falsification: Contest-aware decisions degrade league rankings or cannot be predicted across different opponent styles.

rules.title: Change priorities with body size, density and game phase
rules.if_state: Current length, percent of occupied arena, nearest head distance and elapsed turn change the distribution of observed 10-turn deaths and pre-death food events.
rules.then_hypothesis: Evaluate adaptive length/occupancy/phase priorities against simpler fixed weights, not presume a particular weight schedule from observational rate differences.
rules.counterexample: Long snakes are typically present in crowded boards, and strong opponents differ across games: an apparent state effect can be a length, skill or scheduling confounder. No observed grouping identifies a winning intervention.
rules.next_experiment: Check pre-action interaction predictions on fully held-out whole games/seasons, then perform adaptive versus fixed-weight agent ablations across diverse fresh opponents and paired seeds.
rules.falsification: Adaptive priorities fail to improve first place, retained length and death rate on fresh league-like matches relative to a fixed-weight agent.

rules.title: Promote only decisions that transfer to diverse league opposition
rules.if_state: A candidate feature or move rule looks promising on trials or a small set of replayed opponents.
rules.then_hypothesis: Require distinct game, season and bot-version holdouts and league-like controlled ablations before promotion.
rules.counterexample: A top trial bot can be weak in student competition, and repeated hourly snapshots may reuse one seed and old bot version.
rules.next_experiment: Design a frozen diverse peer-opponent panel and held-out seeds; benchmark first-place frequency, retained growth, death rate and timeout.
rules.falsification: The candidate loses performance on previously unused peer opponents or fresh league-like seeds.
